scope: Required behaviors for eventual real Oracle and cross-backend acceptance; scenarios are not proof of execution

cases.description: Email and username login succeed with valid bcrypt; absent or wrong credentials are 401, inactive account is 403 and issues no session.
Successful login returns complete self user and signed tokens with matching HttpOnly cookies; session hashes and JTI, device fields and last_login are correct.
Missing 2FA schema is reported safely and never bypasses second-factor checks.
Enabled 2FA on an untrusted device returns a 300-second challenge with no session, login cookies or last_login update.
Valid TOTP or unused recovery code consumes the active challenge once and issues the full session; replay and concurrent use are rejected.
Remembered device is managed with the same data fields and expiration; revoked or expired device is not trusted.
New-device notification and configured email side effects follow existing rules; failures do not log raw secrets or block successful login.
Profile and close failures never send new auth cookies; earlier auto-committed writes are recorded as potentially persisted.
All backends run the shared public bcrypt vectors including 72-byte and Unicode compatibility.
Cross-backend login, challenge completion, refresh and logout work with a shared isolated Oracle and signing keys, from both Web and Flutter clients.

After checking the old password, let reset commit before the login lock is acquired. Direct login and trusted-device login both return 401 without inserting a session or setting cookies; an untrusted device gets no new challenge.
Let password login commit its session first, then commit reset. The issued access and refresh credentials are rejected after reset.

Issue a challenge and trust a device for one account, then commit a password reset. The old challenge returns 401; logging in with the new password and old fingerprint requires a new factor challenge. Other accounts retain their credentials.

Let a factor completion load its credential, consume its challenge, and pause before creating device trust. Commit reset and resume the completion. It returns 401 without setting cookies, creating a session or restoring trust.

Connect an existing session to a separate WebSocket instance and commit a password reset. The next incoming application frame (including malformed input), protected outbound delivery, or idle revalidation closes the socket after observing the revoked row.
